gtshaders.ai.opt_max_tokens_hint: Max output tokens per call. "auto" sends no limit and lets the server use the model's own maximum - recommended. If you set one, remember reasoning counts against it too
gtshaders.ai.pitfall.absolute_threshold: Heads up: it uses a hard-coded luma threshold and may vanish in the dark
gtshaders.ai.pitfall.bad_annotation: Heads up: a @param annotation failed to parse and will be missing from the panel
gtshaders.ai.pitfall.game_time: Heads up: it drives animation from GameTime, which wraps and cannot be paused
gtshaders.ai.pitfall.no_frag_color: Heads up: fragColor is never assigned, so the output is undefined
gtshaders.ai.pitfall.one_shot: Heads up: it ramps GTTime once, so the effect may already be over
gtshaders.ai.pitfall.packed_bilinear: Note: reads bit-packed data with texture(); filtering destroys the bit pattern
gtshaders.ai.pitfall.reserved_name: Heads up: a parameter name collides with a built-in
gtshaders.ai.pitfall.screen_size_texel: Heads up: it derives texel size from ScreenSize instead of OutSize
gtshaders.ai.pitfall.too_few_params: Heads up: this effect has almost nothing to tweak
gtshaders.ai.pitfall.unused_param: Heads up: a declared parameter is never used - its slider will do nothing
gtshaders.ai.protocol_hint: OpenAI and DeepSeek speak Responses; Zhipu, Kimi, Bailian, SiliconFlow, OpenRouter and local models speak Chat. Picking the wrong one gives a 404
gtshaders.ai.provider_add: Add an entry: from a preset, or copy the current one
gtshaders.ai.provider_incomplete: This entry still needs a base URL and a model
gtshaders.ai.provider_label_placeholder: Name this entry so you can tell them apart
gtshaders.ai.reverted: The last round broke it; reverted to the previous working version
gtshaders.ai.stage.generating_blocking: Generating... (streaming off - waiting for the whole reply)
gtshaders.ai.stage.polishing: Compiled - fixing patterns that would make the effect invisible...
gtshaders.ai.stage.repairing: Compile failed - letting it fix itself (round %s of %s)
gtshaders.ai.title: Generate with AI
gtshaders.ai.wish_placeholder: e.g. raindrops sliding down a window, glass slightly blurred
gtshaders.anchor.check.no_slot: earlier bindings used up every slot, so this one gets none — lower their Max Slots, or move this binding up
gtshaders.anchor.check.occluded: but it is occluded (visibility=0), so most effects fade out — turn off this binding's occlusion test, or move somewhere with line of sight
gtshaders.anchor.check.persistent: "%s" is a persistent anchor (slot #%s) and needs no trigger — here is its state right now
gtshaders.anchor.check.slot_unread: no effect layer reads slot #%s — pick "%s" in the effect's Anchor Binding parameter
gtshaders.anchor.check.unresolved: but no target resolved: check the selector, whether the target is in view, and the Max Distance setting
gtshaders.anchor.emitter_unused: No layer reads gtEmitter, so nothing here will change the picture
gtshaders.anchor.empty: No bindings yet. Add one and your effect can anchor to an entity or a world position instead of covering the whole screen.
gtshaders.anchor.export_note: Anchors are written by the mod every frame. Exported as a plain resource pack there is nothing writing them, so every anchor goes invalid and the effect falls back to its screen-space form. For world anchors on a vanilla client, use gtProbe instead.
gtshaders.anchor.facing_target_hint: Targets without a look vector (block pos, look hit) fall back to the angles below
gtshaders.anchor.go_bind: Go bind (close UI, pick with crosshair)
gtshaders.anchor.hint.block_pos: Block position as x,y,z. The anchor sits at the block centre.
gtshaders.anchor.hint.entity_type: Entity type id, e.g. zombie or minecraft:zombie. Namespace optional.
gtshaders.anchor.hint.entity_uuid: Entity UUID. Look at the target in game and press the pick key (Home) to fill it in.
gtshaders.anchor.hint.held_item: Item id. Entities holding it in either hand are matched.
gtshaders.anchor.hint.item_entity: Item id; leave empty to match every dropped item.
gtshaders.anchor.name: Name
gtshaders.anchor.pick_no_binding: Add a binding on the Anchors tab first
gtshaders.anchor.quick.full: All anchor slots are in use
gtshaders.anchor.quick.no_layer: No layer reads anchors yet - add "Laser Strike" from the library
gtshaders.anchor.quick.no_project: Open the editor once with Insert to create a project
gtshaders.anchor.trigger_disabled: "%s" is disabled - enable it in the anchor panel first
gtshaders.anchor.usage_overflow: Slots are taken by the bindings above, so this one never fires. Lower their max slots, or move this binding up.
gtshaders.anchor.warn.duration: Duration 0 = persistent; the effect stays on its final frame
gtshaders.anchor.warn.source: This source can never fire an event trigger

gtshaders.core.error.no_frag_color: No fragColor assignment in the vanilla template; this kind does not support the automatic fragment hook
gtshaders.core.error.no_main: No void main() in the vanilla template, so nothing can be injected
gtshaders.core.error.no_position: No gl_Position expression in the vanilla template; this kind does not support the automatic vertex hook
gtshaders.core.error.nothing_to_export: There are no core shaders to export
gtshaders.core.missing_assets: Vanilla shaders for Minecraft %s are missing. Put them under %s and try again
gtshaders.core.template.const_params: Note: core shader parameters are compiled as const, so changing one means regenerating the shader.
gtshaders.core.template.fragment_hook: Fragment hook: changes the final color. Returning it unchanged leaves it as is.
gtshaders.core.template.hooks_only: Only write the functions below; GTShaders generates the rest from the vanilla template.
gtshaders.core.template.vertex_hook: Vertex hook: changes the vertex position. Returning it unchanged leaves it as is.
gtshaders.debug.busy: The previous sample is still being read
gtshaders.debug.err.bad_expr: The expression cannot contain semicolons, braces, comments or line breaks
gtshaders.debug.err.comment_line: Line %s is inside a comment or preprocessor directive
gtshaders.debug.err.empty_expr: Nothing to watch: put the caret on a variable or select an expression
gtshaders.debug.err.layer: Debugging works on enabled post-processing layers only
gtshaders.debug.err.line_range: Line %s is out of range (%s lines)
gtshaders.debug.err.no_layers: No enabled post-processing layer to inspect
gtshaders.debug.err.not_statement: Line %s does not end a complete statement (inside parentheses, in a multi-line expression, or right before else)
gtshaders.debug.err.outside_function: Line %s is not inside a function body
gtshaders.debug.err.timeout: Sampling timed out: nothing is being rendered (e.g. not in a world)
gtshaders.debug.inexact: The main buffer is not 8-bit RGBA; readings may be inexact.
gtshaders.debug.inspect_hint_layers: Click anywhere on the view to read that pixel before effects and after every layer. The view flickers for a few frames and the timeline pauses.
gtshaders.debug.inspect_hint_ub: Check active: click the view to read the first problem at that pixel and its line.
gtshaders.debug.inspect_hint_value: Probe active: click the view to read the exact value of the expression at that pixel (bitwise readback, not an 8-bit approximation).
gtshaders.debug.need_layer: Select an enabled post-processing layer first.
gtshaders.debug.not_hit: This pixel never reached the probed line (skipped by a branch, or outside the viewport).
gtshaders.debug.probe_hint: Fastest way: put the caret on a variable in the code area and press Ctrl+E. The view turns into a false-color map of that value, taken the first time each pixel reaches the line.
gtshaders.debug.probe_legend: Scalars: blue→cyan→green→yellow→red maps the low to the high end of the range; vectors show as RGB. Gray checkerboard = not reached, magenta = NaN, white = infinity.
gtshaders.debug.probe_on: Probe on: the view shows this value; click to read exact numbers
gtshaders.debug.profiler_hint: Measures one frame every 0.4 s: the real GPU time of each layer. A full bar is 16.7 ms, one whole frame at 60 FPS.
gtshaders.debug.profiler_unsupported: This GPU or render backend does not support timestamp queries.
gtshaders.debug.profiler_waiting: Waiting for the first round… (if data never arrives, the timing hook did not apply on this machine)
gtshaders.debug.ub.clamp: clamp with min greater than max
gtshaders.debug.ub.pow: pow out of range (negative base, or zero base with exponent ≤ 0)
gtshaders.debug.ub.smoothstep: smoothstep with equal edges (division by zero)
gtshaders.debug.ub_hint: Replaces pow, sqrt, log, asin, smoothstep, clamp, normalize and mod, whose results are undefined for out-of-range arguments, with checked versions, and checks the output for NaN / infinity. These behave differently across GPUs: looking fine here does not mean it looks fine elsewhere.
gtshaders.debug.ub_legend: Magenta = argument out of range, yellow = output is NaN or infinite; other pixels are dimmed.
gtshaders.debug.ub_on: Check on: highlighted pixels had a problem; click one to see the line
gtshaders.doc.CameraBlockPos: Vanilla Globals: integer block position of the camera
gtshaders.doc.CameraOffset: Vanilla Globals: fractional offset of the camera inside that block; add it to CameraBlockPos for the camera's world position
gtshaders.doc.GTDeltaTime: Frame delta in seconds. Editor only; always 0 in a resource pack
gtshaders.doc.GTFrame: Frame counter. Editor only; always 0 in a resource pack
gtshaders.doc.GTLayerIndex: Index of this layer among enabled layers (0-based)
gtshaders.doc.GTPlaying: 1 while the timeline plays, 0 when paused; always 1 in a resource pack
gtshaders.doc.GTTime: Time in seconds. Follows the pausable editor timeline; in a resource pack it is the vanilla game clock, wrapping every 1200 s
gtshaders.doc.GTViewportUV: Normalized coordinates inside the viewport frame; use it to make the effect follow the frame
gtshaders.doc.GameTime: Vanilla Globals: fraction of the current day, 0..1
gtshaders.doc.InSampler: Main color buffer: the image this layer reads (the previous layer's output; the world for the first layer)
gtshaders.doc.InSize: Size of the input buffer in pixels
gtshaders.doc.OutSize: Size of this pass's output buffer in pixels; one pixel is 1.0 / OutSize
gtshaders.doc.ScreenSize: Vanilla Globals: window size in pixels; use OutSize for the pixel size of a pass
gtshaders.doc.fragColor: Color written by this layer; branches that never write it keep the original image
gtshaders.doc.gl_FragCoord: Window coordinates of the current pixel; pixel centers are at +0.5
gtshaders.doc.texCoord: Screen UV, 0..1, origin at the bottom-left

gtshaders.driver.off_hint: Turn the driver off and go back to manual control
gtshaders.driver.on_hint: Animate this parameter over time (written into the source annotation, so it also works in exported packs)

gtshaders.export.name: File name

gtshaders.export.pack_view_hint: When on, every uniform the preview receives matches a plain resource pack: time follows the vanilla clock (wraps every 1200 s, freezes when paused), anchors / emitters / trails are zero. The shader source is identical either way.
gtshaders.export.parity_count: %s input(s) have no source in a pack (see README)

gtshaders.outline.glow_on: %s now glows locally (only you can see it)
gtshaders.outline.layer_note: This layer replaces the vanilla minecraft:entity_outline chain and only affects glowing entities. It can read both the per-entity silhouette mask and the main image, but has no blend mode — the engine composites it with a fixed alpha blend.
gtshaders.outline.need_glowing: The outline chain only runs while something is glowing. Press PageUp to glow the entity under your crosshair, or use /effect give <target> minecraft:glowing
gtshaders.outline.no_glow_warning: Nothing is glowing in view, so this layer will not run

gtshaders.panel.texture_pick_hint: Click to cycle through the built-in icon and PNGs you dropped into the editor

gtshaders.param.anchor_raw: By number #%s (does not follow binding order)
gtshaders.param.compact_hint: Click for a slider · Ctrl+click to type a value
gtshaders.param.inferred: (range and type guessed from the name; add a // @param line to pin them)
gtshaders.param.reset_hint: Restore every parameter on this layer to the author's default
gtshaders.parity.anchors: world anchors (gtAnchor*) — falls back to screen-space form
gtshaders.parity.camera: world camera (gtWorldPos / gtLinearDepth) — distance still works, but world-locked geometry follows the view
gtshaders.parity.system: %s — constant in a pack (delta 0, frame 0, playing 1)
gtshaders.right.bilinear_hint: Sample between texels. Blur-like effects need it; per-pixel effects don't care
gtshaders.right.core_scope_hint: Every object of this kind is affected - a resource pack cannot single one out.
gtshaders.right.viewport_core_na: Core shaders are not bounded by a region; the settings below do not apply.
gtshaders.right.viewport_post_only: The settings below only affect post-process layers, not core shaders.
gtshaders.right.world_clock_hint: Replaces the vanilla GameTime with the timeline above, so core shader layers follow play/pause too — they read GameTime directly, and without this only post layers stop. The cost is that vanilla animation everywhere (water, portals) freezes as well.
gtshaders.right.world_clock_pack_view: Inactive in pack view: that simulates a player loading a plain resource pack, where time must come from the vanilla clock. Turn pack view off to restore it.

gtshaders.scan.drive_float_only: Line %s, parameter %s: drivers only work on float parameters; ignored

modmenu.descriptionTranslation.gtshaders: In-game visual editor for Minecraft shaders: post-processing and 21 kinds of vanilla core shaders, with live preview, auto-detected parameters and one-click export to resource packs that work without the mod.
modmenu.summaryTranslation.gtshaders: In-game shader editor with live preview and one-click resource pack export.
